items.title: A finite morphism with a singleton fibre is locally determined near the point, with finite local rings and matching stalks
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: For a finite morphism pi : X -> Y and x over y with pi^{-1}({y}) = {x}, the lemma proves four statements: neighbourhoods of x in X are approximated by full inverse images of neighbourhoods of y; the local ring map O_{Y,y} -> O_{X,x} is finite; it is of finite presentation when pi is; and for every quasi-coherent module F the stalk F_x equals (pi_*F)_y as O_{Y,y}-modules. The retained proof is written: the topological statement from continuity plus closedness of finite maps with the single-point fibre; parts (2), (3) by affinization to a finite ring map A -> B where the fibre condition makes q the unique prime over p, applying Algebra, lemma-unique-prime-over-localize-below to identify B_q = B_p so the local map is a plain localization (details the author marks as simple properties of localization); part (4) computed by the same localization identity plus an alternative direct stalk argument via part (1). Retained author proof at lines 13570-13591.
